notes: On 7 October 2021, representatives of local committees opposing coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions gathered outside the Madonna dei Sette Dolori Church in Pescara (Pescara, Abruzzo) to ask for the acknowledgment of their position from regional authorities.
On 5 January 2022, around 100 delivery riders on motorcycles staged a ride protest in Bristol to demand more protection from violence and harassment they suffered while working.

On 28 March 2023, between 260 (according to the police) and 300 (unions) demonstrators took to the streets in Elbeuf. The event was part of a tenth national and cross-sector day of strike and demonstration called by eight unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and five student organizations (UNEF, VL, FIDL, FAGE, and MNL) to oppose the passing of a pension reform bill by means of Article 49.3 of the constitution by the government, and call for the withdrawal of the bill.

On 28 October 2023, during the afternoon, around 500 people gathered in the district St. Georg in Hamburg - Hamburg-Mitte for a spontaneous pro-Palestine demonstration. Clashes broke out with police officers who used tear gas. 2 police officers were injured.
On 8 March 2025, 1,300 people protested in Jaen (Andalucia) to demand gender equality on the occasion of International Women's Day.

On 12 February 2021, a group of Bologna branch USB, We Remain, Power To The People, Communist Network and PRC party affiliates took part in a sit-in outside the Emilia-Romagna Region headquarters in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna) to call for universal access to the coronavirus vaccine as well as patent-free vaccine-related research.

On 25 May 2021, Priority to School affiliates and supporters and representatives of the school branch of the CGIL trade union gathered outside the Regional School Office (USR) in Florence (Firenze, Toscana) to demand more security guarantees against coronavirus infections in schools for the next school year, including the recruitment of more school staff, the commitment to reduce class sizes and more investments in school infrastructure.
On 26 October 2024, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Lidkoping, Vastra Gotaland, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 26 August 2023, people, called by the Platform in Defense of a Decent Health of the Basic Health Zone of Tabara, staged a massive protest in Tabara (Zamora, Castilla y Leon) demanding better health care services, including employing more health care professionals so that the health centers operate 24/7 and offer specialist patient care.
On 9 May 2025, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Linkoping, Ostergotland, to draw attention to environmental issues and to demand action against climate change.

On 10 June 2023, at the call of the alliance 'Ingolstadt is colorful', numerous people, including members of FFF, Antifa, elected officials (The Greens, The Left), a protestant pastor, and the mayor (SPD), demonstrated on Carraraplatz in Ingolstadt against historical revisionism, fascism, far-right extremism, and an event of the revisionist association ZFI - Ingolstadt Research Institute for Contemporary Historical Research.
On 30 October 2020, activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Przeworsk protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 18 February 2024, around 80 people, including representatives of ADFC, BUND, NABU, 'Climate decision Duisburg' (Klimaentscheid Duisburg), The Left, The Greens and Volt Europa, participated in a cycling protest in Duisburg (Nordrhein-Westfalen) against the tree policies of the city administration and the felling of trees. They argued that although preserving the trees was costly, it was worth it from a climate perspective.

On 29 August 2024, striking employees of the Youth Judicial Protection (PJJ) sector, including CGT members, demonstrated in Nimes (Occitanie) against a national social plan including a redundancy plan that foresaw the non-renewal of 500 contracts from 1 September 2024. This nationwide action was called by the inter-union SNPES-PJJ/FSU, CGT, UNSA SPJJ, and CFDT.

On 7 April 2021, market vendors from across the Cosenza province gathered, at the call of the ANA and UGL trade unions, outside the Stefano Rizzo stadium in Rossano (Cosenza, Calabria) to protest against continued coronavirus restrictions to their activities and demand a clear roadmap for the reopening of their businesses from public authorities.

On 9 September 2020, around 1,000 people protested in Kiel for the reception of refugees from the Greek refugee camp Moria in which a fire had broken out the previous night. The protest was organised by Seebruecke.

On 7 December 2024, at the call of CAAR - Anti-Racist Counter-Attack Collective (Collectif Contre-Attaque Anti-Raciste), more than 60 people gathered in Grasse (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to support a woman named Carolle and her family, who claim to have endured years of racism from their neighbors, and raise awareness on the persistence of racism and demand justice.
On 2 March 2022, people gathered in Eskilstuna to denounce the Russian invasion of Ukraine and call on authorities to promote peace.
On 8 May 2020, about 50 people protested in Straubing. The exact reason for the protest was not reported, but it is likely in connection with the coronavirus lockdown measures.
On 6 September 2020, local residents protested in Kraljske Bare, Montenegro, against construction of a mini hydro power plant, citing environmental concerns.
Around 19 July 2020, (as reported) around 400 people protested in Rottenburg am Neckar for the preservation of a slaughterhouse at its current location.

On 12 March 2024, at the call of Lurzaindia, more than 150 people, including farmers and CP (ELB) affiliates, gathered outside the Court of Justice in Bayonne (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to express solidarity with four Ostia affiliates who were on trial for damaging a Bouygues agency during a demonstration in 2023. The demonstrators also protested against the planned construction of a housing estate by Bouygues in the locality, which they deemed damaging to the environment.
On 8 March 2024, on the occasion of International Women's Day, around 200 people gathered in Gotha (Thuringen) to protest against patriarchal structures.

On 15 September 2022, students held a protest at the Faculty of Law of the University of Granada in Granada (Andalucia) against the presence of former deputy of Vox Macarena Olona who starred in an act in the Auditorium organized by the Forum of Concord.
On 23 April 2021, environmental activists protested in Hofors to oppose clear-cutting of forests in various areas in Sweden.

On 30 September 2020, around 60 members of the Platform for People Affected by Mortgages (PAH) gathered in Manresa (Barcelona) to complain about the bureaucratic obstacles for registering at the local municipality.

On 5 September 2021, an unknown number of workers from the cultural sector protested at the Formula 1 race track in Zandvoort (Noord-Holland) to demand more attention for the cultural sector in the context of the coronavirus measures of the Dutch government.
On 22 May 2024, at the call of CGT, striking Gepor employees blocked access to the port in Illange (Grand Est) to protest against the sale of their company and demand safe jobs.
On 11 March 2021, health workers protested in Colmar because they are not entitled to a monthly salary increase that hospital health workers have been granted by the Segur agreements.
On 29 September 2020, an unknown number of people staged a protest on Het Plein in Den Haag against the coronavirus protection laws of the Dutch government.

On 20 March 2021, several dozen protesters gathered in Cathedral Square in central Vilnius to demonstrate against coronavirus restrictions, especially compulsory wearing of face masks. An MP from the opposition Freedom and Justice party was present at the event. The rally was reportedly part of an international movement, which organized protests against coronavirus restrictions on this day in over 50 countries.

On 1 May 2025, people participated in a protest organized by the Socialist Party and the National Congress of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs, marching from the Circus to the Opera and Ballet Theatre in Chisinau - Buiucani. The demonstration was directed against the PAS leadership and the president, calling for social justice and dialogue with Russia. The protest was led by Socialist Party members of Parliament. There are indications that participants were brought to the event via organized transportation. The Soviet song 'Katyusha' was played during the event.

On 11 April 2023, striking NHS junior doctors represented by BMA formed a picket line outside Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge over a pay dispute and working conditions. The event was part of a four-day national industrial action.

On 8 February 2025, around 2,000 teachers, called by the Board of Teaching Staff, protested in Santander (Cantabria) to reject the government's latest salary adjustment proposal, which they deemed insufficient. Protesters criticized the regional government's offer of a 90-euro increase in three installments, while also condemning proposed conditions tying salary increases to attendance, arguing it unfairly penalized teachers on medical leave.
On 12 May 2020, Albanian land workers, who are permanent residents in Imathia [coded to Veroia] participated in a strike-protest demanding an increase of their wages.

On 1 April 2023, 40 anarchist activists took to the streets of Cesena (Emilia-Romagna, Forli-Cesena) to demonstrate in solidarity with Alfredo Cospito, a well-known anarchist currently on hunger strike to demonstrate against the 41-bis prison regime, and 3 other anarchists currently charged with theft, among others, after a 'No Green Pass' demonstration held on 13 November 2021.

On 12 March 2025, students of the Higher School of Electrical Engineering and Computing Vocational Studies gathered in Vojvode Stepe Street in Belgrade - Vozdovac to observe 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign. The aim was to honor the victims and emphasize their demands for the accountability for the loss of 15 lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station.

On 29 May 2021, Belarusian activists gathered for a rally in Biala Podlaska, declaring their solidarity with the political opposition at home and demanding immediate release of journalist Protasevich, who was arrested in Minsk.

On 24 January 2022, campaigners belonging to Stop HS2 and HS2 Rebellion (associated with Extinction Rebellion) demonstrated with banners and a prop elephant called Nelly at Euston station in London - Camden as part of a full day of action against the expansion of the HS2 infrastructure project.

On 26 August 2021, Alitalia airline company workers, including flight attendants, gathered outside the company's former headquarters in Rome - Europa (Roma, Lazio) to demand guarantees for their professional future following the reorganization of Alitalia as ITA.

On 23 November 2022, citizens, summoned by CSIF, held a protest in Malaga (Andalucia) to demand quality public services and denounce deficiencies in health, education, justice, and the Andalusian government.

On 22 October 2020, people, most of them FdI affiliates and including their leader, took part in a flash mob outside of Montecitorio Palace in Rome - City Center to protest against the potential introduction of a second lockdown to face coronavirus infections by the government and denounce the consequences of the public handling of the coronavirus pandemic on certain professional categories.

Around 23 July 2021 (as reported), over 500 people took the street in Palermo (Palermo, Sicilia) to pay tribute to an anti-mafia magistrate killed in the 1992 Via D'Amelio bombing and protest against mafia presence within the state.
On 12 September 2022, around 600 people demonstrated in Kothen for peace in Ukraine and against 'state paternalism' concerning health and other matters.
On 19 November 2021, citizens called by the ADICAE association protested in Zaragoza (Aragon) against the recent increases in power prices.

On 20 June 2020, about 700 people marched through Cobham village in Surrey for a Black Lives Matter protest, demonstrating against police brutality and systemic racism after the killing of an unarmed black man by a police officer in the United States.
On 24 November 2023, people gathered inside Gare du Nord in Paris (Ile-de-France) to express solidarity with the Palestinian people amid the 2023 Israel-Hamas War.

On 7 December 2020, about 20 activists affiliated to the movement Million Moments for Democracy gathered for a rally in Karlovy Vary, protesting against alleged harmful pressure against the media of public service from politicians. They demanded preservation of independence especially of the national TV station Czech Television.
On 19 September 2022, people demonstrated in Greifswald against inflation.

On 20 April 2024, around 25 Last Generation activists gathered in Saarbrucken (Saarland), demanding increased government action on climate change, resulting in 6 participants being taken into custody by the police.

On 20 October 2020, primary care physicians (general practitioners) called by the Malaga Medical Union gathered in Malaga to protest about excessive work overload during the coronavirus pandemic. Protesters demanded more human and material resources be allocated to the public health services.
On 1 March 2019, in Rekovac, Serbia citizens held a protest against the regime of Aleksandar Vucic. This protest was a part of a series of protests happening throughout the country for several weeks.

On 14 September 2024, around 2,500 people participated in the Christopher Street Day (CSD) parade in Dortmund (Nordrhein-Westfalen), to protest for LGBTQ+ rights and visibility. Around 50 right-wing individuals staged a counter-protest nearby, while at the call of Antifa, around 150 left-wing protesters demonstrated against the right-wing protest. The police effectively kept the groups apart. Two right-wing protesters were detained for making homophobic remarks and performing a Hitler salute. In addition, there were minor incidents, including children attempting to throw eggs at CSD participants.

On 21 November 2024, farmers, including CR affiliates, gathered with a dozen tractors in Strasbourg (Grand Est), where they distributed 600 kilograms of apples in a demonstration. The event was part of a nationwide demonstration movement by French farmers opposing the EU-Mercosur trade deal and condemning delays in agricultural reforms promised by the previous government following the winter 2023-2024 farmers' demonstrations.
On 12 December 2020, around 80 persons demonstrated in Clichy. They called for decent housing for undocumented families, housed by the city council in unsanitary hotels.

On 10 November 2020, 16 teachers protested in Auxerre to denounce the government's management of the coronavirus health crisis. They denounced a lack of means and space so that the classes could safely take place. They called for splitting up classes into small groups in middle schools. They also called for more financial, material, and human resources. They also denounced what they perceive as disdain from the government.

On 13 February 2022, citizens called by 'We are not crime platform' protested in Vitoria-Gasteiz, demanding the repeal of the Law on Public Safety. They said that the law limits freedoms and criminalises protest activity. The CNT, CGT, Amnesty International, Ecologists in Action, Greenpeace and CEAR unions and organizations were involved in the demonstration.

On 15 October 2021, in the morning, Electrolux workers gathered, with the support of RSU union representatives, outside their company's gates in Susegana (Treviso, Veneto) to protest against the extension of coronavirus 'green pass' restrictions to public and private sector workers, set to come into force on that day. Vaccinated workers reportedly took part in the protest to express solidarity with their colleagues.

On 7 January 2022, several far-right affiliates gathered in Acca Larentia street in Rome - Tuscolano (Roma, Lazio) to commemorate the victims of the 1978 Acca Larentia killings and denounce the role of the far left in the killings. Demonstrators performed the Fascist salute and several of them did not wear a mask in compliance with coronavirus restrictions. CasaPound took part in the demonstration.

On 24 April 2021, people protested in Plevenon against the failure to carry out votes during the municipal councils due to the resignation of the municipal councilors. They called for the budget to be voted.

On 10 October 2021, people, among them CGIL members, gathered in Reggio Emilia (Reggio nell'Emilia, Emilia-Romagna) to guard the CGIL branch in protest against the far-right assault on the union's headquarters in Rome. The Mayor of Reggio Emilia, a PD MP, Legacoop, and a regional council member took part in the event.

On 25 July 2019, residents of the Aerodrom Municipality in Skopje held a peaceful protest in front of a clinic against the government's decision to treat addicts at this local clinic, fearing the safety of their children.

On 17 December 2021, at the call of CGT and CFDT, around 30 Departmental Center for Children and Families (CDEF) employees gathered outside the Departmental Council in Saint-Brieuc (Bretagne) to protest against the restructuring of their workplace.

On 11 February 2023, between 6,000 (according to the authorities) and 15,000 (according to the unions) people staged a protest march in Morlaix. The event was part of a fourth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 13 July 2024, thousands of LGBTQ+ community members and their supporters marched through Bristol (England) as part of the city's annual pride event, to celebrate the LGBTQIA+ community and campaign on banning conversion therapy and protecting the community's rights.

On 29 July 2022, road construction workers gathered in Blagoevgrad to protests the delays in payment they have been facing for months, as the issue of road construction contracts being politicized sparks a three-day series of protests nationwide. Three-day protests have been organized nationwide and the protesters have announced a wider blockade of the road system in the upcoming months.

On 5 December 2020, between 600 and 1,000 persons demonstrated in Valence. They called for the removal of article 24 of the 'comprehensive security' bill and denounced its potential infringement of the principle of freedom of information, especially on reporting on police brutality. The article criminalizes disseminating images with personal identifiers of a police or military officer, with the aim of affecting his or her physical or psychological integrity.

On 11 December 2024, public employees, called by CCOO, UGT, ANPE, USO, the Federation of Associations of Education Inspectors and Inspecting Officers (Federacion de Asociaciones de Inspectores e Inspectoras de Educacion - ADIDE), the Union of Education Inspectors (Union Sindical de Inspectores de Educacion - USIE), the Federal Police Union (Union Federal de Policia - UFP), ACAIP, and the Independent Union of the Tax Agency (Sindicato Independiente de la Agencia Tributaria - SIAT), held a protest outside Muface offices in Ourense (Galicia) to defend Muface, a mutual healthcare system, against potential integration into the public health system.

On 24 October 2024, activists from the Grandparents' Climate Action (BKA) demonstrated in Askim, Viken, to urge stronger climate action, calling on politicians to take responsibility for future generations by intensifying efforts to combat climate change.
On 1 January 2021, a protest against the government was held in Ljubljana, Slovenia.
On 26 July 2020, around 500 members of the LGBT community protested in Leipzig for their rights under the motto 'The Future is Intersectional - Queer Perspectives'.

On 28 September 2024, pro-Palestinian demonstrators from Eindhoven4Palestine marched through the city center of Eindhoven (Noord-Brabant), starting at the 18 Septemberplein, to protest what they called a genocide in Palestine, and to demand an end to the Israeli occupation and Dutch complicity herein. The march included speeches and a route through the Kleine Berg and followed smaller protests earlier in the week at the technical university of Eindhoven.

On 23 March 2023, hundreds of farmers and fishers, including the president of the Schleswig-Holstein Farmers' Association and members of the Schleswig-Holstein Poultry Association, demonstrated in Busum against the agricultural policy and financial cuts in crab fishing. They also were against the EU Commission's planned ban on bottom trawls in protected areas.
On 24 September 2021, students affiliated with the FFF movement gathered for a rally in Leszno, demanding better protection of the climate.

On 10 January 2025, about 2500 Slovak activists gathered for a rally in Presov, protesting against violations of democratic principles in the country. In particular they criticized the PM's recent unscheduled visit to Russia and asserted their support for Ukraine.
On 14 September 2022, people demonstrated in Tampere to oppose the possible construction of a highway passing through a recreational forest in the area.

On 4 July 2024, nearly 900 protesters and representatives of NFP, SOS Racism, and unions rallied at Horloge Square and subsequently took to the streets in Avignon (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demonstrate. The event was part of a nationwide wave of demonstrations against far-right ideology and in support of an open society, and took place after the National Rally (RN) came first in the European elections in France and President Emmanuel Macron announced the dissolution of the National Assembly on 9 June 2024, prompting snap legislative elections and raising fears of a government led by the far-right party.
On 6 June 2021, local residents gathered in Sodermalm district of Stockholm to demonstrate for preservation of Liljeholmsbadet floating swimming pool that is planned to be closed.
On 1 August 2021, Pro Life activists gathered in Milano - Municipio 1 to protest against legal euthanasia. They claimed it is a form of 'legalized homicide'.

On 22 June 2024, at the call of CNT, striking Acqua hotel maids - most of them women - gathered for a picket line outside the Radisson hotel in Marseille (Provence-Alpes-Cote d'Azur) to demand a pay rise.
On 17 May 2023, about 130 young people protested in Kruibeke, to demand 'space to be young', party venues in the town, and tolerance towards young people.
On 18 June 2021, around 35 employees of the Siap-Prociner company demonstrated in Bassens. They called for equal pay for all employees of the company, regardless of the branch they work for.
On 28 January 2022, Fridays for Future activists demonstrated in Kalmar to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.
On 14 February 2020, a Fridays For Future climate strike gathered in Salo, demanding climate action. No students seemed to be in attendance.

On 22 September 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Oskarshamn, Kalmar, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change. The demonstration was part of the global climate action held on 22 September.

On 24 April 2024, protesters gathered in front of the Ministry of Internal Affairs building in Sofia due to the arrest of journalist Dimitar Stoyanov from Bird BG on what they claim are trumped-up charges of hooliganism and weapons possession. The protest was organized by the BOEC association.

On Mar. 5, 2018: Environmental activists held a rally in Tirana in protest against various construction works in protected and tourist areas. Protesters said they were trying to stop the irreversible destruction of Albanian nature by private firms that violate laws and corrupt judges who helped them.

On 7 September 2024, at the call of Poitiers Palestine, 150 people demonstrated from the town hall to the prefecture in Poitiers (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) in solidarity with Gaza, Palestinians, and their children. They denounced an Israeli army killing a civilian population and defined the country's actions as an '11-month genocide'.
On 22 November 2021, hairdressers protested in Valencia (Valencian community), calling on the government to reduce the VAT rate (from 21% to 10%) applied to their labour sector.

On 23 September 2024, citizens organized by the informal group 'Mirijevo Green and Healthy' protested in Mirijevo in Belgrade - Zvezdara against the planned cutting of 66 hectares of forest near the 'Bajdina' area for to the construction of residential and commercial buildings. The protest was interrupted by individuals claiming to be owners of the plot, who attempted to interrupt the demonstration. The police we called to re-established order and identified those who attempted to interrupt the gathering

On 14 May 2021, pro-Israeli and pro-Palestine activists gathered near the embassy of Israel in Prague, supporting their respective sides in the ongoing conflict. No violent interactions were reported.
On 10 July 2020, anti-government protesters rallied in Maribor, Slovenia. They protested against corruption, as well the government's response to the coronavirus.

On 15 January 2024, around 200 farmers drove their vehicles in Sibiu in protest of the high insurance fees, the high fuel price, and the high taxes. The protesters also demanded a stop to the import of cereals and a review of the agricultural subsidies.

On 4 May 2021, temporary workers and employees of the entertainment and cultural industries, continued the occupation of a theater in Le Havre. They protested against the forced closure of the arts sector due to coronavirus-related measures implemented by the government and against unemployment benefit reforms.

On 12 October 2023, employees of the Bulgarian mining and energy sector protested in Sliven against plans to close down regional power plants in the country, part of a coal phaseout plan that they claim will leave many jobless.

On 9 February 2023, around 200 workers of the Huesca City Council held a protest in Huesca (Aragon) against the loss of the seniority supplement, which had been paid for over 30 years and received by more than 300 municipal employees.
On 17 April 2023, several hundred nurses and other health workers gathered for a rally in Katowice, demanding higher wages and other social benefits.

On 1 May 2021, citizens protested in Palencia, including CCOO and UGT, calling for a fair way out from the health and economic crisis caused by the coronavirus pandemic on International Labor Day. They demanded the government to assign priority to the social agenda.

On 31 January 2025, health workers gathered in front of the Betanija Maternity Hospital in Novi Sad to observe 15 minutes of silence as part of the 'Serbia, Stop' campaign, to honor the victims who lost their lives following the collapse of a concrete canopy at the Novi Sad train station and demand accountability for their deaths.

On 1 February 2022, around 20 health workers and professionals of the medico-social sector demonstrated in Auch, at the call of 6 unions (CFE-CGC, CGT, FSU, SUD, CNT, FO). They denounced their working conditions and called for an increase of their salaries.
On 12 May 2023, Fridays For Future activists demonstrated in Vasteras, Vastmanland, to draw attention to environmental problems and to demand action against climate change.

On 13 August 2022, at the call of S.I. COBAS, security and reception workers of Eurospin supermarkets held a protest in Parma (Parma, Emilia-Romagna) to demand a wage increase and regularization of part-time contracts, sickness and leave policies.

On 15 June 2024, 80 people demonstrated in Montluel (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes) to demand a ceasefire in Gaza, express solidarity with the Palestinian people, and condemn what they deemed a 'genocide' of Gazans by the Israeli army.

On 5 October 2023, more than 1000 demonstrators, mostly students, demonstrated in Helsinki to oppose the government's proposed cuts to services that could affect students' welfare. Activists protested against planned cuts to housing allowances, a freeze on the indexation of student grants and increases in tuition fees for non-EU/EEA students.
On 10 December 2022, residents of Plovdiv protested against plans to build a high-rise building along the river in the city, which would cut down on the green space in the area.

On 21 August 2023, pensioners gathered in Tetovo to demand a linear or equal increase of pensions, claiming that inflation and the high cost of living eat away at their budget. Protests were organized in several Macedonian cities and towns.

On 10 January 2022, students from middle schools, elementary schools, and various high schools including Sannazaro, Vittorini and Caro in Napoli (Napoli, Campania), staged a demonstration against the reopening of schools with in-presence classes without safer studying conditions amid a spike in the coronavirus cases, as it is not possible to keep physical distance among students. But they also were opposed to online classes as the conditions for access are not provided by the government nor considered an adequate solution to children's welfare.

On 1 June 2024, at the call of PvdD, about 20 people protested in front of the Vion slaughterhouse in Tilburg (Noord-Brabant) against animal suffering. The protesters set up a cross to symbolize death in front of a tree nearby.

On 18 May 2020, around 30 citizens marched to protest in Pamplona by banging pots against the management of the coronavirus crisis by the Government. Protesters also called for the Government to resign.
Around 19 November 2021 (as reported), at the call of the CP, farmers gathered in front of a supermarket in Millau, to denounce the measures adopted by the government against the bird flue.
On 5 December 2023, at the call of STC, around 100 municipal workers gathered in Ajaccio (Corse) to demand a pay rise.
On 8 October 2020, members of Oxford Friends of the Earth rallied in Botley calling for urgent action to cut the 'unacceptable' levels of pollution across Oxfordshire.
On 27 October 2018, 2018 in Croatia's capital Zagreb the Animal Liberation Initiative organized an international protest to ban hunting, attended by activists from several countries.
On 18 October 2022, around 100 bakers staged a protest outside the cabinet of the Wallonian Minister of Economy in Namur to demand governmental support for their rising energy costs.

On 11 July 2022, a group of farmers staged a protest action in Barneveld, blocking the road with tractors while hanging up reversed Dutch flags throughout the town to denounce the new Dutch nitrogen regulations.

On 13 January 2024, several hundred people, including Palestinian ambassador Salah Abdel Shafi, participated in a pro-Palestine protest in Vienna - Inner City (Wien 1-Innere Stadt) to call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire.
On 12 August 2021, protesters gathered in Viljandi to oppose plans to cut approximately 50 trees to build a sidewalk and bicycle path along a street in the city center.

On 10 February 2022, in the evening, three municipal officials gathered in downtown Manfredonia (Foggia, Puglia) to protest against the increase in commodity prices. The event was part of a national evening of protest, by which municipalities briefly turned off the light of their landmarks' facades, organized by ANCI.
On 20 June 2020, health workers gathered in Malaga to claim for a better public health scheme. Protestors demanded more material and economic resources amid coronavirus pandemic.

On 23 February 2023, about 30 residents of the Lavino neighborhood in Anzola dell'Emilia gathered in Bologna (Bologna, Emilia-Romagna), outside the oratory San Filippo Neri where a conference on land consumption sponsored by the city of Bologna was being held, to protest against the construction of a supermarket in a green area in Lavino. Legambiente representatives were among the demonstrators against the project which, in addition to damage pristine soil, is likely to soar pollution levels due to envisaged traffic increase.

On 1 April 2025, 15 temporary security workers staged a protest at the San Francesco d'Assisi Airport in Perugia (Umbria) against the outsourcing of security services by Sase, the airport management company, due to a reduction in wages due to the new company's application of a less favorable contract.

On 21 March 2025, at the call of USB, striking call center workers employed by Assocontact staged a picket outside the headquarters of Confcommercio in Taranto (Puglia) to protest against their working conditions, the new contract proposed to workers, the wage and benefits reduction the new deal entails, and the practice of contractual dumping.
On 23 February 2025, several hundred activists gathered in Wroclaw for a rally in front of the local consulate of Ukraine, protesting against the presence of the so-called Azov battalion in the city.

On 9 July 2022, 7 XR activists occupied an ING bank office in Den Bosch (Noord-Brabant) to denounce the bank's investments in fossil fuels. Five activists who stayed after the bank's closing time were arrested by the police.

On 22 June 2024, people, including local elected officials and women, gathered in Hasparren (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to condemn gender-based violence after a woman was raped during the local fair the day prior.

On 16 September 2020, a dozen private health workers gathered with banners in front of the Confindustria offices in Bologna to protest against the non-renewal of their national contract. The demonstration was organized by the Labor Unions CGIL, CISL and UIL.

On 6 September 2020, protesters against a regulation obliging children to wear face masks when they return to school as part of the government's coronavirus measures rallied in Arta. The protesters, who were holding Greek national flags and comprised of a diverse crowd including parents, members of the anti-vaccine movement and Orthodox Christian religious groups organised in social media, stamped on face masks and burned them, while chanting slogans against the Prime Minister.
On 24 October 2020, several hundred activists, mostly women, gathered for a rally in Warsaw, protesting against restrictions of abortions in Poland. The event was coordinated by the Women's Strike.

On 16 March 2023, an unknown number of people assembled in Nimes to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform bill and its decision to pass it through the use of the Article 49.3 of the French Constitution.

On 30 March 2024, residents of Novi Beograd and activists marched and blocked the road in Belgrade - Novi Beograd, voicing their dissatisfaction with the local government's plans to build a skyscraper within the green areas of this part of the city.

On 28 March 2021, around 150 environmental activists protested in Montelimar to call on the government to implement concrete measures to tackle climate change. Protesters denounced that the climate and resilience bill was not stringent enough to meet the 2030 greenhouse gas emission reduction target. They also called for the 149 proposals from the Citizens Convention for Climate to be implemented. The event was part of a national day of protest called by Greenpeace, Friends of the Earth, International Movement ATD Fourth World, Attac, CARE, CCFD-Terre Solidaire (Catholic Committee against hunger and for development), XR, L214, FAGE, France Nature Environnement (French Nature Environment), Generations Futures (Future Generations), LDH, LPO - Ligue pour la protection des oiseaux (League for the Protection of Birds), Notre affaire a tous (Everyone's Business), OXFAM, SDN, EELV, Generation Ecologie (Ecology Generation), CFDT, and PS, before consideration by parliament of the government's climate and resilience bill, which they criticized.
On 20 January 2022, around 100 No Tav activists gathered in Trento (Trento, Trentino-Alto Adige) against the preliminary works of the Trento railway ring road.
On 22 January 2022, at the call of ecologist groups, nearly 400 persons demonstrated in Amiens to raise awareness about the environmental and social consequences of global warming.

On 26 February 2024, farmers and supporters staged a protest in Frankfurt (Oder) (Brandenburg), blocking the city bridge with some vehicles and causing traffic disruptions. The protest aimed to address agricultural concerns and was part of a nationwide demonstration movement against the federal coalition government and its agricultural policies.

On 24 September 2024, at the call of FNADEPA - National Federation of Associations of Directors of Establishments and Services for the Elderly (Federation Nationale des Associations de Directeurs d'Etablissements & Services pour Personnes Agees), residents, their families, and employees gathered outside the Abbaye elderly home (EHPAD) in Grenoble (Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes). The event was part of a nationwide strike and demonstration movement of elderly home residents and employees called by FNAAFP - Federation of Directors of Establishments for the Elderly (Federation des Directeurs d'Etablissements pour Personnes Agees) and named 'The Elderly Deserve More' (Les Vieux Meritent Mieux) to demand more financial funding and better services in their sector.

On 7 September 2019, several hundred people in Valjevo, Serbia, protested over a gathering which was supposed to show support for the upcoming Belgrade Pride march. The original gathering was then cancelled.

On 23 September 2021, 150 teachers demonstrated in Saint-Brieuc, at the call of unions (CGT, FO, Sud, SNES-FSU). They denounced their working conditions and demanded for an increase of their emoluments.
On 12 September 2022, 80-100 people, mostly students and teachers, protested outside the Deak Ferenc school in Szeged in support of the teachers' strike for better wages and more teaching staff.

On 11 July 2020, over two hundred people gathered in Reggio Calabria (Reggio di Calabria, Calabria) under the banner 'Let's Remain Free' to protest against a draft law against homotransphobia. Protesters claimed that such a law would affect their freedom of expression, education, religion, social and political aggregation.

On 7 March 2023, an unknown number of people staged a protest in Caen. The event was part of a sixth national and cross-sector day of strike and protest called by unions (CFDT, CGT, FO, CFE-CGC, CFTC, UNSA, SUD, and FSU) and students' organizations to oppose the government's pension and retirement age reform.

On 5 May 2024, around 100 people took to the streets to demonstrate in Pau (Nouvelle-Aquitaine). The event was part of a nationwide demonstration day called by 800 organizations, including LGBTQ+ collectives, feminist associations, PS, MFPF, AUP, The Ecologists, SUD, NPA, NT, SOS Homophobie, and LFI, to condemn transphobia after the publication of a Senate LR-championed bill on transidentity and the promotion of the book 'Transmania', both of which the protesters deemed transphobic.

On 14 November 2022, activists from Extinction Rebellion staged a protest outside of a branch of Barclays bank at Clapham junction in London - Wandsworth, calling for the bank to end its investment in the fossil fuel industry. This event was part of the national day of action against Barclays bank.

On 8 June 2020, at least 10 African and other foreign students organised by VOIS (Voices of International Students in Cyprus) rallied outside TRNC parliament in northern Nicosia to express their solidarity with the United States Black Lives Matter demonstrators and to protest against racist practices in Northern Cyprus. The students were also supported by representatives of LGBT groups.

On 5 November 2021, around 500 people, including former workers of Whirlpool's Neapolitan plant, S.I. COBAS affiliates, road maintenance workers and unoccupied people, some of them affiliated with the local '7 November' and 'New Benches' movements, gathered outside the Prefecture, in Plebiscito square, in Napoli (Napoli, Campania) to demand answers regarding their professional future and ask to meet with the Labor Minister, visiting the city's mayor on that day. At least one umbrella was thrown at a police cordon standing outside the Prefecture, generating tension.
On 15 August 2022, residents held a protest in front of the Gijon Bullring in Gijon (Asturias) in favor of the return of the bulls to the city. The protest was summoned by Pena Taurina Gijona.

On 17 June 2020, around 1500 people staged a protest at Haarlemmerhout in Haarlem against racism and police violence in the context of worldwide Black Lives Matter protests. Kick Out Zwarte Piet took part in the protest.

On 10 October 2024, lawyers gathered outside the Court of Justice in Agen (Nouvelle-Aquitaine) to express solidarity with all persecuted lawyers worldwide, notably imprisoned Tunisian Lawyer Sonia Dahmani.
On 15 August 2022, around 70 people demonstrated in Grossenhain against coronavirus-related measures as they gathered for a 'Monday Walk' - name given to such demonstration.

On 21 August 2021, around 1,700 persons demonstrated in Quimper. They called for the withdrawal of a coronavirus-related bill on the obligation to provide the proof of the double vaccination to resume their professional and social activities.

On 11 July 2019, more than a thousand former workers of the 'Aluminij' company, mainly ethnic Croatians, and their supporters demonstrated in front of the Croatian Democratic Union (HDZ) headquarters in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina. Two people were arrested after an object was thrown at HDZ's president's car.
